c.identity: Small C syscall-table read probe / regression fixture
c.verdict_basis: The entire 346-byte source contains one READ_KERN(syscall_table_addr[syscall_num]) expression; the result and string pointers are discarded. No process-memory write, GOT modification, shellcode execution, or memfd_create call exists. The memfd marker is an ordinary local identifier. Injection-related string literals alone do not implement injection.
c.context_limit: No complete build or deployment purpose is supplied. Kernel introspection is dual-use; this incomplete read-only stub has no concrete hostile effect.

inc.identity: INC Windows x86-64 ransomware, compiled with Rust/MinGW
inc.verdict_basis: Executable file traversal/encryption, encoded INC extortion note, deliberate termination of file holders and processes/services, shadow-copy deletion, and quiet-mode timestamp restoration establish ransomware independently of reputation or classifier score.
execution_trace: 0x402490 traverses files, excludes operating-system/application paths and executable/library extensions, writes ransom notes, and queues targets.
0x403c30 initializes per-file cryptographic state and overlapped file processing; 0x404b60 captures original file times and 0x404c43 reads file contents.
Worker code dispatches buffer transformation through 0x413d50, whose loops XOR data against generated stream blocks; 0x405126 restores saved file times under a configuration flag.
0x403480 enumerates volumes, opens device paths and invokes DeviceIoControl with 0x53c028, then selects the success/error shadow-copy deletion log.
0x40c070 enumerates/terminates processes; 0x40cc20 calls ControlService; 0x40d170 uses Restart Manager resource registration/listing/shutdown and process termination to release file holders.
0x4101f4 loads the Base64 note at VA 0x5c7249, passes it to decoder 0x407330, and stores the recovered note. A separate note-writing path at 0x4018d0 constructs INC-README.txt.
Generic connect and CreateProcessW paths occur in Rust networking/process support. Their import co-occurrence does not bind received network data to command execution.
inc.context_limit: No runtime execution, operator authorization or deployment history is supplied. The extortion note claims stolen data; the reviewed binary paths do not independently establish exfiltration or a reusable backdoor, and no such detection was added.

stx.verdict_basis: CLI registration and handlers perform build/serve/deploy and component generation. Dynamic Function construction compiles template expressions; subprocess paths run build tools, local Craft hosts, and platform browser openers. Native APIs expose documented clipboard/media/device features, configured logging, autostart helpers and signature verification. These behaviors fit the framework purpose, without an identified covert theft, destruction or tasking path.

provenance.verification: Forager fetched the exact published scoped package/version; SHA-256 is byte-identical to the supplied artifact. Its .forage.json provenance remains in scratch.

execution_trace: dist/cli.js registers explicit CLI handlers; the deploy handler invokes Bun.spawn(["bun","run","build"]) in the project directory.
chunk-j6x7ryyn.js emits client runtime/template compilation and configured fetch hooks; Function construction is used for expressions and cloned-component setup.
chunk-8md2707p.js creates Bun development/HMR servers, serves project files and opens the local URL.

chunk-zwkc8yge.js delegates to configured native Craft bridges or launches the resolved local Craft binary. Base64 helpers carry binary/media data and signature material; crypto.subtle verifies Ed25519 signatures. Configured logging POSTs entries to the caller-provided endpoint.
dist/native/text-entry.d.ts:26 contains autocomplete="current-password" only in an explanatory comment about native form vocabulary. It sets no credential field and captures no password.
stx.context_limit: Actual consuming applications and native permission grants are unavailable. This verdict concerns the supplied published tarball; it does not grant trust to every application built with the framework or every separately fetched dependency.

corrections_and_coverage: Moved code-cave, shellcode-writing and GOT-writing literals to metadata/lang/source/literal at notable; the matcher supports references, not injection effects. Removed unsupported ATT&CK/MBC mappings from those literals.

Required lseek/write call evidence for real source injection. Moved the generic descriptor-write/shellcode profile to micro-behaviors/process/inject/memory; retained actual code-cave/GOT hijack detections on upstream TripleCross.

Removed native-winsock-host-check-command-agent: generic host, socket and process APIs establish no connected-command agent. Retained every constituent API finding; a neutral process-completion API profile preserves the two otherwise-orphaned baseline wait/exit-code facts.

Moved termination logs/options/control groups into process and service capability homes. Individual process/service success logs do not prove masked termination; distinct real masked-success strings now supply the mask observations.

Required extortion/encryptor context for the hostile termination controls and moved them from ransom/affiliate to impact/degrade/process and impact/degrade/services. Generic logging, shutdown, mask options and a speed switch alone cannot establish ransomware.

Moved ordinary username/password autocomplete text into ui/window/form-input, removed OWA theft mappings, and updated the OWA objective to reference neutral attributes. Descriptions explicitly record text rather than field creation or credential access.
Added general Base64 extortion phrases covering all three byte alignments. The publication matcher requires ransom nonpayment plus disclosure, rather than a generic publication statement.

Added native file-encryption/extortion, shadow-copy recovery inhibition and timestamp-restoration detections. Raw/hex help matchers recover relevant bytes omitted by text extraction because they share a long merged run with the encoded note. No hashes, chosen filenames, C2 hostnames or exact sample sizes gate these detections.

shared_consumer_audit.disposition: The Empire injection selector is PowerShell-scoped, so the changed C/C++ evidence cannot supply it. Generic autofill text must not serve credential-access legs in MCP/config or webhook-theft composites; true OWA capture still fires in a positive control. CrystalX uses broad C2/impact selectors as exclusions; inaccurate C2 evidence must leave that set, while true ransomware impact remains. No broad selector was expanded to reintroduce neutral observations as intent.
shared_consumer_audit.positive_source: Upstream TripleCross src/user/include/utils/mem/code_caver.h, fetched through Forager from h3xduck/TripleCross; byte-identical positive fixture is included with SHA-256 in check.py.
shared_consumer_audit.positive_before_after: TripleCross retains both hostile code-cave and GOT-hijack findings. Its generic descriptor profile remains suspicious in its neutral injection home. The network-attack command-marker PE control and OWA capture source control retain their hostile findings. The generated PE returns immediately and tests static matching only.

regression_result: 15 controls passed, including a real injector, no-write/no-seek near misses, ordinary/OWA autofill, generic Windows imports, command-agent tasking, ordinary encryptor and termination logs, encoded-note-only controls and all three Base64 alignments.
detection_losses: No supported observation was lost on the three supplied artifacts: literal/autofill/log observations were relocated, two wait APIs retained, and the unsupported reference-only injection and import-only backdoor claims were removed. The corrected termination objectives retain ransomware coverage with required extortion context. Final member-by-member differences are recorded under samples.
remaining_disagreements: None at the current atomscan alert threshold. C changes from HOSTILE to BENIGN; INC remains HOSTILE; STX is BENIGN both before and after this local reasoned-review comparison, despite the queue prior. Scores and calibrated levels are recorded, not treated as behavioral evidence.
classifier_limit: Atomscan warns that its v18 feature spec predates the v21 extractor. Verdicts here are independently supported by source and native-code review.
validation_command: make validate (required final action; outcome reported in final response)
marker_status: Exactly one requested verdict marker per supplied sample was written and verified before final validation.
